3. المتغيّر skip يفرض افتراضاً غير مبرر على توزيع القطاعات ويؤدي إلى أخطاء عندما تكون j تقع خارج النطاق المتوقّع. 
4. الكود يخلط بين منطق البحث عن الفروع (ulist, dlist) وإجراءات القفز، مما يجعل الفهم والصيانة شبه مستحيلة. 
5. لا يتم التعامل مع حالة عدم وجود j‑th تبديلة بشكل واضح (يُطبع -1 فقط إذا كان j ≥ cnt[C][N]، وهذا صحيح). 
6. لا توجد تعليقات توضيحية ولا تقسيم واضح للوظائف.
بشكل عام، يمكن تبسيط الحل إلى جزأين واضحين: (أ) حساب جدول cnt مرة واحدة لكل اختبار، (ب) معالجة كل استفسار عبر دالة findValue(i, j) التي تتبع المسار في شجرة الخيارات باستخدام cnt فقط، دون الحاجة إلى القفزات المعقّدة.

<|write_code|>
مسألة جديدة: اكتب برنامجاً يقرأ t اختبارات، لكل اختبار يقرأ n, c, q، المصفوفة p، ثم q استفسار (i, j). يجب طباعة العنصر i في j‑th تبديلة أو -1 إذا لم توجد. الحل يعتمد على حساب cnt مسبقاً ثم استعراض المسار.
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;
using int64 = long long;
const int64 INF = (int64)2e18;   // حد أعلى لتجنب overflow

// cnt[k][len] = عدد التبديلات الممكنة لجزء بطول len بميزانية k
vector< vector<int64> > cnt;

void precompute(int maxC, int maxN){
    cnt.assign(maxC+1, vector<int64>(maxN+1,0));
    for(int k=0;k<=maxC;k++) cnt[k][0]=1; // جزء فارغ
    for(int k=0;k<=maxC;k++){
        for(int len=1; len<=maxN; ++len){
            int64 sum=0;
            for(int d=0; d<=min(k,len); ++d){ // d = طول القطعة المعكوسة (0 يعني لا نعيد شيء)
                sum += cnt[k-d][len-d];
                if(sum>INF) { sum=INF; break; }
            }
            cnt[k][len]=sum;
        }
    }
}

// دالة تساعد على إيجاد قيمة العنصر i (0‑based) في j‑th تبديلة (0‑based)
int answer_query(const vector<int>& p, int n, int C, int i, int64 j){
    if(j >= cnt[C][n]) return -1; // لا توجد تبديلة بهذا الرقم
    int pos = 0;          // الموضع الحالي في المصفوفة الأصلية
    int budget = C;       // الميزانية المتبقية
    while(pos < n){
        // 1) الخيار: لا نعيد أي قطاع (نمر على العنصر كما هو)
        int64 ways_no_rev = cnt[budget][n-pos-1]; // بعد تخطي العنصر الحالي
        if(j < ways_no_rev){
            // العنصر i يقع في هذا الفرع إذا i==pos
            if(i == pos) return p[pos];
            ++pos; // ننتقل للعنصر التالي
            continue;
        }
        j -= ways_no_rev; // نتخطى جميع التبديلات التي لا تبدأ بقطعة عند pos
        // 2) نحاول اختيار قطاع بطول d (1..budget) يبدأ من pos
        bool found = false;
        for(int d=1; d<=budget && pos+d<=n; ++d){
            int64 ways = cnt[budget-d][n-pos-d]; // بعد عكس قطاع بطول d
            if(j < ways){
                // العنصر i يقع داخل هذا القطاع المعكوس أم بعده؟
                if(i >= pos && i < pos+d){
                    // داخل القطاع، نحسب موقعه بعد العكس
                    int rev_idx = pos + d - 1 - (i - pos);
                    return p[rev_idx];
                }
                // العنصر بعد القطاع، ننتقل إلى الموضع بعده
                i -= d; // لأننا حذفنا d عناصر من البداية بالنسبة للمؤشر الأصلي
                pos += d;
                budget -= d;
                found = true;
                break;
            }
            j -= ways; // نتخطى هذا الطول d
        }
        if(!found){
            // لا توجد قطاعات أخرى، وهذا يعني أن j كان غير صالح (يجب ألا يحدث)
            return -1;
        }
    }
    return -1; // غير متوقع
}

int main(){
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int T; cin>>T;
    // الحد الأقصى للـ n عبر جميع الاختبارات ≤ 3e5، والحد الأقصى للـ c هو 4
    const int MAXC = 4;
    const int MAXN = 300000; // حسب القيد العام
    precompute(MAXC, MAXN);

    while(T--){
        int n, C, q; cin>>n>>C>>q;
        vector<int> p(n);
        for(int i=0;i<n;++i) cin>>p[i];
        while(q--){
            int i; long long j; cin>>i>>j; // i 1‑based, j 1‑based في النص الأصلي
            --i; --j; // تحويل إلى 0‑based
            int ans = answer_query(p, n, C, i, j);
            cout<<ans<<"\n";
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```
هذا البرنامج يحقق التعقّـد O(n·c) لتجهيز cnt مرة واحدة، ثم لكل استفسار يعمل في O(n) في أسوأ الحالات (مع c ≤ 4 يصبح الفحص سريعاً). يمكن تحسينه إلى O(n) ثابت عبر تخزين القفزات، لكن بما أن c صغير وعدد الاستفسارات كبير، الأداء يكفي ضمن الحدود المطلوبة.

original_problem_description:
Alice had a permutation p_1, p_2, …, p_n. Unfortunately, the permutation looked very boring, so she decided to change it and choose some non-overlapping subranges of this permutation and reverse them. The cost of reversing a single subrange [l, r] (elements from position l to position r, inclusive) is equal to r - l, and the cost of the operation is the sum of costs of reversing individual subranges.     cin >> T;
```cpp
    while (T--) {
        int n; 
        cin >> n;
        vector<int> tag(n);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> tag[i];
        vector<long long> s(n);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> s[i];

        vector<long long> dp(n, 0); // أعلى نقاط عند الانتهاء من المسألة i
        long long ans = 0;

        for (int j = 1; j < n; ++j) {
            for (int i = j - 1; i >= 0; --i) {
                if (tag[i] == tag[j]) continue;
                long long w = llabs(s[i] - s[j]);
                long long dpi = dp[i];
                long long dpj = dp[j];
                dp[i] = max(dp[i], dpj + w);
                dp[j] = max(dp[j], dpi + w);

            }
        }

    }
    return 0;
}
```

It's guaranteed that sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 5000.

```java
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        long q = Long.parseLong(br.readLine().trim());

        // حالة 1 أو عدد أولي
        if (q == 1) {
            System.out.println(1);
            System.out.println(0);
            return;
        }
        List<Long> primes = primeFactors(q);
        // إذا كان عدد العوامل الأولية هو 1 (q هو عدد أولي)
        if (primes.size() == 1) {
            System.out.println(1);
            System.out.println(0);
            return;
        }
        // إذا كان عدد العوامل الأولية يساوي 2 (p أو p*p أو p*r)
        if (primes.size() == 2) {
            System.out.println(2);
            return;
        }
        // أكثر من عاملين: اللاعب الأول يربح ويختار أول عاملين
        System.out.println(1);
        long move = primes.get(0) * primes.get(1);
        System.out.println(move);
    }

    // إرجاع قائمة بالعوامل الأولية (مع التكرار) للعدد n
    private static List<Long> primeFactors(long n) {
        List<Long> list = new ArrayList<>();
        long d = 2;
        while (d * d <= n) {
            while (n % d == 0) {
                list.add(d);
                n /= d;
            }
            d = (d == 2) ? 3 : d + 2; // تخطي الأعداد الزوجية بعد 2
        }
        if (n > 1) {
            list.add(n);
        }
        return list;
    }
}
```

original_problem_description:
You can't possibly imagine how cold our friends are this winter in Nvodsk! Two of them play the following game to warm up: initially a piece of paper has an integer q. During a move a player should write any integer number that is a non-trivial divisor of the last written number. Then he should run this number of circles around the hotel. Let us remind you that a number's divisor is called non-trivial if it is different from one and from the divided number itself. 

The first person who can't make a move wins as he continues to lie in his warm bed under three blankets while the other one keeps running. Determine which player wins considering that both players play optimally. If the first player wins, print any winning first move.

Input

The first line contains the only integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 1013).

Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specificator.

Output

In the first line print the number of the winning player (1 or 2). If the first player wins then the second line should contain another integer — his first move (if the first player can't even make the first move, print 0). If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

Examples

Input

6


Output

2


Input

30


Output

1
6


Input

1


Output

1
0

Note

Number 6 has only two non-trivial divisors: 2 and 3. It is impossible to make a move after the numbers 2 and 3 are written, so both of them are winning, thus, number 6 is the losing number. A player can make a move and write number 6 after number 30; 6, as we know, is a losing number. Thus, this move will bring us the victory.

مسألة جديدة: احسب أقصى طول لمقطع متتالي في الدائرة الأولى يكون تسلسلاً فرعياً في الدائرة الثانية بعد اختيار نقاط القطع بشكل أمثل.
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main(){
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int la, lb;
    if(!(cin>>la>>lb)) return 0;
    vector<int> A(la);
    vector<int> B(lb);
    for(int i=0;i<la;i++) cin>>A[i];
    for(int i=0;i<lb;i++) cin>>B[i];

    // خريطة من قيمة الهيروغليف إلى موقعه في B (إذا وجد)
    const int MAXV = 1000000 + 5;
    vector<int> posInB(MAXV, -1);
    for(int i=0;i<lb;i++) posInB[B[i]] = i;

    // سنمر على A مرتين (لف الدائرة) لتغطية جميع القطاعات الممكنة
    // ونبني سلسلة من المواضع في B (مع إضافة lb عند الحاجة لللف)
    vector<int> seq; // ستحمل المواضع المتزايدة
    int best = 0;
    // نستخدم تقنية LIS مع "patience sorting"
    vector<int> tails; // tails[i] أصغر قيمة يمكن أن تنتهي بها سلسلة بطول i+1

    // نمر على A مرتين لتغطية جميع القطاعات المتتالية التي قد تتجاوز طول A
    for(int start=0; start<la; ++start){
        tails.clear();
        // نعيد بناء السلسلة من الموضع start إلى start+la-1
        for(int k=0; k<la; ++k){
            int idx = (start + k) % la;
            int val = A[idx];
            int p = posInB[val];
            if(p==-1) continue; // غير موجود في B
            // لتجنب مشكلة اللف، نضيف نسخة من p مع إزاحة lb إذا لزم الأمر
            // نبحث عن أصغر موضع أكبر من آخر موضع استخدمناه في tails
            // نستخدم binary_search على tails لتحديد الموضع المناسب
            // لكن يجب أن نسمح بزيادة p ب multiples of lb عندما لا يكون ممكنًا الزيادة مباشرة
            // أبسط طريقة: نحتفظ بمتغير lastPos يوضح آخر موضع تم اختياره في B (مع الإزاحة)
            // ثم نضيف إما p أو p+lb بحيث يكون أكبر من lastPos
            static int lastPos; // سيُعاد تعيينه لكل بداية جديدة
            if(k==0) lastPos = -1; // بداية جديدة
            int cur = p;
            if(cur <= lastPos) cur += ((lastPos - cur) / lb + 1) * lb; // رفع إلى أعلى مستوى
            // الآن cur > lastPos
            // نضيف cur إلى LIS التقليدي (لكن بما أن القيم الآن مرتبة تصاعديًا تلقائيًا، فإن طول LIS هو عدد العناصر المتتالية)
            // لذلك يمكن ببساطة زيادة الطول
            // لكن لنحافظ على العامة، نستخدم tails كما في LIS العادي
            auto it = lower_bound(tails.begin(), tails.end(), cur);
            if(it==tails.end()) tails.push_back(cur);
            else *it = cur;
            lastPos = cur;
        }
        best = max(best, (int)tails.size());
    }

    cout<<best<<"\n";
    return 0;
}
```

original_problem_description:
Polycarpus enjoys studying Berland hieroglyphs. Once Polycarp got hold of two ancient Berland pictures, on each of which was drawn a circle of hieroglyphs. We know that no hieroglyph occurs twice in either the first or the second circle (but in can occur once in each of them).

Polycarpus wants to save these pictures on his laptop, but the problem is, laptops do not allow to write hieroglyphs circles. So Polycarp had to break each circle and write down all of its hieroglyphs in a clockwise order in one line. A line obtained from the first circle will be called a, and the line obtained from the second one will be called b.

There are quite many ways to break hieroglyphic circles, so Polycarpus chooses the method, that makes the length of the largest substring of string a, which occurs as a subsequence in string b, maximum.

Help Polycarpus — find the maximum possible length of the desired substring (subsequence) if the first and the second circles are broken optimally.

The length of string s is the number of characters in it. If we denote the length of string s as |s|, we can write the string as s = s1s2... s|s|.

A substring of s is a non-empty string x = s[a... b] = sasa + 1... sb (1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ |s|). For example, "code" and "force" are substrings of "codeforces", while "coders" is not. 

A subsequence of s is a non-empty string y = s[p1p2... p|y|] = sp1sp2... sp|y| (1 ≤ p1 < p2 < ... < p|y| ≤ |s|). For example, "coders" is a subsequence of "codeforces".

Input

The first line contains two integers la and lb (1 ≤ la, lb ≤ 1000000) — the number of hieroglyphs in the first and second circles, respectively.

Below, due to difficulties with encoding of Berland hieroglyphs, they are given as integers from 1 to 106.

The second line contains la integers — the hieroglyphs in the first picture, in the clockwise order, starting with one of them.

The third line contains lb integers — the hieroglyphs in the second picture, in the clockwise order, starting with one of them.

It is guaranteed that the first circle doesn't contain a hieroglyph, which occurs twice. The second circle also has this property.

Output

Print a single number — the maximum length of the common substring and subsequence. If at any way of breaking the circles it does not exist, print 0.

Examples

Input

5 4
1 2 3 4 5
1 3 5 6


Output

2


Input

4 6
1 3 5 2
1 2 3 4 5 6


Output

3


Input

3 3
1 2 3
3 2 1


Output

2

Note

In the first test Polycarpus picks a string that consists of hieroglyphs 5 and 1, and in the second sample — from hieroglyphs 1, 3 and 5.

original_problem_description:
Valeric and Valerko missed the last Euro football game, so they decided to watch the game's key moments on the Net. They want to start watching as soon as possible but the connection speed is too low. If they turn on the video right now, it will "hang up" as the size of data to watch per second will be more than the size of downloaded data per second.

The guys want to watch the whole video without any pauses, so they have to wait some integer number of seconds for a part of the video to download. After this number of seconds passes, they can start watching. Waiting for the whole video to download isn't necessary as the video can download after the guys started to watch.

Let's suppose that video's length is c seconds and Valeric and Valerko wait t seconds before the watching. Then for any moment of time t0, t ≤ t0 ≤ c + t, the following condition must fulfill: the size of data received in t0 seconds is not less than the size of data needed to watch t0 - t seconds of the video.

Of course, the guys want to wait as little as possible, so your task is to find the minimum integer number of seconds to wait before turning the video on. The guys must watch the video without pauses.

Input

The first line contains three space-separated integers a, b and c (1 ≤ a, b, c ≤ 1000, a > b). The first number (a) denotes the size of data needed to watch one second of the video. The second number (b) denotes the size of data Valeric and Valerko can download from the Net per second. The third number (c) denotes the video's length in seconds.

Output

Print a single number — the minimum integer number of seconds that Valeric and Valerko must wait to watch football without pauses.

Examples

Input

4 1 1


Output

3


Input

10 3 2


Output

5


Input

13 12 1


Output

1

Note

In the first sample video's length is 1 second and it is necessary 4 units of data for watching 1 second of video, so guys should download 4 · 1 = 4 units of data to watch the whole video. The most optimal way is to wait 3 seconds till 3 units of data will be downloaded and then start watching. While guys will be watching video 1 second, one unit of data will be downloaded and Valerik and Valerko will have 4 units of data by the end of watching. Also every moment till the end of video guys will have more data then necessary for watching.

In the second sample guys need 2 · 10 = 20 units of data, so they have to wait 5 seconds and after that they will have 20 units before the second second ends. However, if guys wait 4 seconds, they will be able to watch first second of video without pauses, but they will download 18 units of data by the end of second second and it is less then necessary.

```python
import sys

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return
    it = iter(data)
    t = int(next(it))
    results = []
    for _ in range(t):
        a = int(next(it))
        b = int(next(it))
        c = int(next(it))
        # عدد مرات العملية الثانية
        op2 = min(b, c // 2)
        b -= op2  # نُبقي ما تبقى من الكومة الثانية
        # عدد مرات العملية الأولى
        op1 = min(a, b // 2)
        total = 3 * (op1 + op2)
        results.append(str(total))
    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(results))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
```

```python
        op2 = min(b, c // 2)
        b -= op2  # نُبقي ما تبقى من الكومة الثانية
        # عدد مرات العملية الأولى
        op1 = min(a, b // 2)
        total = 3 * (op1 + op2)
        results.append(str(total))
    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(results))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
```

```cpp
// من المصدر src مع تجاهل العقدة المحظورة forbid.
long long countReachable(int src, int forbid, const vector<vector<int>>& g) {
    vector<char> visited(g.size(), 0);
    stack<int> st;
    st.push(src);
    visited[src] = 1;
    long long cnt = 0; // لا نعد العقدة src نفسها
    while (!st.empty()) {
        int u = st.top();
        st.pop();
        for (int v : g[u]) {

            if (!visited[v]) {
                visited[v] = 1;
                st.push(v);
                ++cnt;                         // كل عقدة جديدة نصل إليها تُعدّ
            }
        }
    }
    return cnt; // عدد العقد التي يمكن الوصول إليها من src دون المرور بـ forbid
}
```

There are n cities in Berland and some pairs of them are connected by two-way roads. It is guaranteed that you can pass from any city to any other, moving along the roads. Cities are numerated from 1 to n.

Two fairs are currently taking place in Berland — they are held in two different cities a and b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n; a ≠ b).

Find the number of pairs of cities x and y (x ≠ a, x ≠ b, y ≠ a, y ≠ b) such that if you go from x to y you will have to go through both fairs (the order of visits doesn't matter). Formally, you need to find the number of pairs of cities x,y such that any path from x to y goes through a and b (in any order).

The following m lines contain descriptions of roads between cities. Each of road description contains a pair of integers u_i, v_i (1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ n, u_i ≠ v_i) — numbers of cities connected by the road.

```cpp
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> tag[i];
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> s[i];

        vector<long long> dp(n+1, 0); // أفضل نقاط تنتهي عند المسألة i
        long long ans = 0;

        // نمر على جميع الأزواج (i, j) حيث i < j
        for (int j = 2; j <= n; ++j) {
            for (int i = j-1; i >= 1; --i) {
                if (tag[i] == tag[j]) continue; // لا يمكن الانتقال إذا كانت العلامة متساوية
                long long w = llabs(s[i] - s[j]); // الوزن = |s_i - s_j|
                long long dpi = dp[i];
                long long dpj = dp[j];
                // الانتقال i -> j يضيف w إلى المسار الذي كان ينتهي عند i
                dp[j] = max(dp[j], dpi + w);
                // الانتقال j -> i يضيف w إلى المسار الذي كان ينتهي عند j
                dp[i] = max(dp[i], dpj + w);
                ans = max({ans, dp[i], dp[j]});
            }
        }
        cout << ans << '\n';
    }
    return 0;
}
```

```java
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        FastScanner fs = new FastScanner(System.in);
        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(new BufferedWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(System.out)));
        int t = fs.nextInt();
        while (t-- > 0) {
            int k = fs.nextInt();
            int n = fs.nextInt();
            int m = fs.nextInt();
            int[] a = new int[n];
            int[] b = new int[m];
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) a[i] = fs.nextInt();
            for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) b[i] = fs.nextInt();

            List<Integer> ans = new ArrayList<>();
            int i = 0, j = 0;
            boolean possible = true;
            while (i < n || j < m) {
                boolean took = false;
                // أولوية للمنوكارب إذا كان عمله ممكنًا
                if (i < n && a[i] == 0) {
                    ans.add(0);
                    k++;
                    i++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (j < m && b[j] == 0) {
                    ans.add(0);
                    k++;
                    j++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (i < n && a[i] <= k) {
                    ans.add(a[i]);
                    i++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (j < m && b[j] <= k) {
                    ans.add(b[j]);
                    j++;
                    took = true;
                }
                if (!took) { // لا يمكن تنفيذ أي خطوة
                    possible = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!possible) {
                out.println(-1);
            } else {
                for (int idx = 0; idx < ans.size(); idx++) {
                    out.print(ans.get(idx));
                    if (idx + 1 < ans.size()) out.print(' ');
                }
                out.println();
            }
        }
        out.flush();
    }

    // قارئ سريع للمدخلات
    static class FastScanner {
        private final BufferedReader br;
        private StringTokenizer st;
        FastScanner(InputStream is) {
            br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(is));
        }
        String next() throws IOException {
            while (st == null || !st.hasMoreElements()) {
                String line = br.readLine();
                if (line == null) return null;
                st = new StringTokenizer(line);
            }
            return st.nextToken();
        }
        int nextInt() throws IOException { return Integer.parseInt(next()); }
    }
}
```

original_problem_description:
Monocarp and Polycarp are learning new programming techniques. Now they decided to try pair programming.

It's known that they have worked together on the same file for n + m minutes. Every minute exactly one of them made one change to the file. Before they started, there were already k lines written in the file.

Every minute exactly one of them does one of two actions: adds a new line to the end of the file or changes one of its lines.

Monocarp worked in total for n minutes and performed the sequence of actions [a_1, a_2, ..., a_n]. If a_i = 0, then he adds a new line to the end of the file. If a_i > 0, then he changes the line with the number a_i. Monocarp performed actions strictly in this order: a_1, then a_2, ..., a_n.

Polycarp worked in total for m minutes and performed the sequence of actions [b_1, b_2, ..., b_m]. If b_j = 0, then he adds a new line to the end of the file. If b_j > 0, then he changes the line with the number b_j. Polycarp performed actions strictly in this order: b_1, then b_2, ..., b_m.

Restore their common sequence of actions of length n + m such that all actions would be correct — there should be no changes to lines that do not yet exist. Keep in mind that in the common sequence Monocarp's actions should form the subsequence [a_1, a_2, ..., a_n] and Polycarp's — subsequence [b_1, b_2, ..., b_m]. They can replace each other at the computer any number of times.

Let's look at an example. Suppose k = 3. Monocarp first changed the line with the number 2 and then added a new line (thus, n = 2, \: a = [2, 0]). Polycarp first added a new line and then changed the line with the number 5 (thus, m = 2, \: b = [0, 5]).

Since the initial length of the file was 3, in order for Polycarp to change line number 5 two new lines must be added beforehand. Examples of correct sequences of changes, in this case, would be [0, 2, 0, 5] and [2, 0, 0, 5]. Changes [0, 0, 5, 2] (wrong order of actions) and [0, 5, 2, 0] (line 5 cannot be edited yet) are not correct.

Input

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Then t test cases follow. Before each test case, there is an empty line.

Each test case contains three lines. The first line contains three integers k, n, m (0 ≤ k ≤ 100, 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100) — the initial number of lines in file and lengths of Monocarp's and Polycarp's sequences of changes respectively.

The second line contains n integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n (0 ≤ a_i ≤ 300).

The third line contains m integers b_1, b_2, ..., b_m (0 ≤ b_j ≤ 300).

Output

For each test case print any correct common sequence of Monocarp's and Polycarp's actions of length n + m or -1 if such sequence doesn't exist.

Example

Input


5

3 2 2
2 0
0 5

4 3 2
2 0 5
0 6

0 2 2
1 0
2 3

5 4 4
6 0 8 0
0 7 0 9

5 4 1
8 7 8 0
0


Output

0 2 0 6 5 
-1
0 6 0 7 0 8 0 9
-1

original_problem_description:
Valeric and Valerko missed the last Euro football game, so they decided to watch the game's key moments on the Net. They want to start watching as soon as possible but the connection speed is too low. If they turn on the video right now, it will "hang up" as the size of data to watch per second will be more than the size of downloaded data per second.

The guys want to watch the whole video without any pauses, so they have to wait some integer number of seconds for a part of the video to download. After this number of seconds passes, they can start watching. Waiting for the whole video to download isn't necessary as the video can download after the guys started to watch.

Let's suppose that video's length is c seconds and Valeric and Valerko wait t seconds before the watching. Then for any moment of time t0, t ≤ t0 ≤ c + t, the following condition must fulfill: the size of data received in t0 seconds is not less than the size of data needed to watch t0 - t seconds of the video.

Of course, the guys want to wait as little as possible, so your task is to find the minimum integer number of seconds to wait before turning the video on. The guys must watch the video without pauses.

Input

The first line contains three space-separated integers a, b and c (1 ≤ a, b, c ≤ 1000, a > b). The first number (a) denotes the size of data needed to watch one second of the video. The second number (b) denotes the size of data Valeric and Valerko can download from the Net per second. The third number (c) denotes the video's length in seconds.

Output

Print a single number — the minimum integer number of seconds that Valeric and Valerko must wait to watch football without pauses.

Examples

Input

4 1 1


Output

3


Input

10 3 2


Output

5


Input

13 12 1


Output

1

Note

In the first sample video's length is 1 second and it is necessary 4 units of data for watching 1 second of video, so guys should download 4 · 1 = 4 units of data to watch the whole video. The most optimal way is to wait 3 seconds till 3 units of data will be downloaded and then start watching. While guys will be watching video 1 second, one unit of data will be downloaded and Valerik and Valerko will have 4 units of data by the end of watching. Also every moment till the end of video guys will have more data then necessary for watching.

In the second sample guys need 2 · 10 = 20 units of data, so they have to wait 5 seconds and after that they will have 20 units before the second second ends. However, if guys wait 4 seconds, they will be able to watch first second of video without pauses, but they will download 18 units of data by the end of second second and it is less then necessary.

original_problem_description:
A string is called a k-string if it can be represented as k concatenated copies of some string. For example, the string "aabaabaabaab" is at the same time a 1-string, a 2-string and a 4-string, but it is not a 3-string, a 5-string, or a 6-string and so on. Obviously any string is a 1-string.

You are given a string s, consisting of lowercase English letters and a positive integer k. Your task is to reorder the letters in the string s in such a way that the resulting string is a k-string.

Input

The first input line contains integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 1000). The second line contains s, all characters in s are lowercase English letters. The string length s satisfies the inequality 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 1000, where |s| is the length of string s.

Output

Rearrange the letters in string s in such a way that the result is a k-string. Print the result on a single output line. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

If the solution doesn't exist, print "-1" (without quotes).

Examples

Input

2
aazz


Output

azaz


Input

3
abcabcabz


Output

-1

```java
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        long q = Long.parseLong(br.readLine().trim());

        // استخراج العوامل الأولية مع تكرارها
        List<Long> primes = new ArrayList<>();
        long n = q;
        for (long d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) {
            while (n % d == 0) {
                primes.add(d);
                n /= d;
                if (primes.size() > 2) break; // لا نحتاج أكثر من ثلاثة عوامل
            }
            if (primes.size() > 2) break;
        }
        if (n > 1) primes.add(n);

        int cnt = primes.size();
        if (cnt <= 1) { // q = 1 أو عدد أولي
            System.out.println(1);
            System.out.println(0);
        } else if (cnt == 2) { // بالضبط عاملين أوليين
            System.out.println(2);
        } else { // ثلاثة عوامل أو أكثر
            System.out.println(1);
            long move = primes.get(0) * primes.get(1); // أول مقسِّم غير تافه
            System.out.println(move);
        }
    }
}
```

original_problem_description:
You can't possibly imagine how cold our friends are this winter in Nvodsk! Two of them play the following game to warm up: initially a piece of paper has an integer q. During a move a player should write any integer number that is a non-trivial divisor of the last written number. Then he should run this number of circles around the hotel. Let us remind you that a number's divisor is called non-trivial if it is different from one and from the divided number itself. 

The first person who can't make a move wins as he continues to lie in his warm bed under three blankets while the other one keeps running. Determine which player wins considering that both players play optimally. If the first player wins, print any winning first move.

Input

The first line contains the only integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 1013).

Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specificator.

Output

In the first line print the number of the winning player (1 or 2). If the first player wins then the second line should contain another integer — his first move (if the first player can't even make the first move, print 0). If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

Examples

Input

6


Output

2


Input

30


Output

1
6


Input

1


Output

1
0

Note

Number 6 has only two non-trivial divisors: 2 and 3. It is impossible to make a move after the numbers 2 and 3 are written, so both of them are winning, thus, number 6 is the losing number. A player can make a move and write number 6 after number 30; 6, as we know, is a losing number. Thus, this move will bring us the victory.

<|explain_concept|>
نستعمل خوارزمية دمج «غريزية» (greedy) تشبه دمج قائمتين مرتبتين. نحتفظ بمؤشرين i و j على بداية كل قائمة. في كل خطوة نتحقق من الفعل التالي في كل قائمة: إذا كان صفرًا نختاره فورًا لأن الإضافة لا تحتاج إلى شرط. إذا كان غير صفر نتحقق إذا كان ≤ عدد الأسطر الحالية k. إذا كان أحد الفعلين قابلًا نختاره (يمكن اختيار الأصغر لتقليل فرص الفشل). إذا لم يكن أي منهما قابلًا فإن النتيجة غير ممكنة ونطبع -1.

<|review_code|>

```java
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        FastScanner fs = new FastScanner(System.in);
        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(new BufferedWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(System.out)));
        int t = fs.nextInt();
        while (t-- > 0) {
            int k = fs.nextInt();
            int n = fs.nextInt();
            int m = fs.nextInt();
            int[] a = new int[n];
            int[] b = new int[m];
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) a[i] = fs.nextInt();
            for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) b[i] = fs.nextInt();

            List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<>();
            int i = 0, j = 0;
            boolean possible = true;
            while (i < n || j < m) {
                boolean took = false;
                // أولوية الإضافة (الصفر) لأنها لا تحتاج إلى شرط
                if (i < n && a[i] == 0) {
                    result.add(0);
                    k++;
                    i++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (j < m && b[j] == 0) {
                    result.add(0);
                    k++;
                    j++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (i < n && a[i] <= k) {
                    result.add(a[i]);
                    i++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (j < m && b[j] <= k) {
                    result.add(b[j]);
                    j++;
                    took = true;
                }
                if (!took) { // لا يمكن تنفيذ أي فعل الآن
                    possible = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!possible) {
                out.println(-1);
            } else {
                for (int idx = 0; idx < result.size(); idx++) {
                    out.print(result.get(idx));
                    if (idx + 1 < result.size()) out.print(' ');
                }
                out.println();
            }
        }
        out.flush();
    }

    // قارئ سريع للمدخلات
    static class FastScanner {
        private final BufferedReader br;
        private StringTokenizer st;
        FastScanner(InputStream is) {
            br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(is));
        }
        String next() throws IOException {
            while (st == null || !st.hasMoreElements()) {
                String line = br.readLine();
                if (line == null) return null;
                st = new StringTokenizer(line);
            }
            return st.nextToken();
        }
        int nextInt() throws IOException { return Integer.parseInt(next()); }
    }
```

original_problem_description:
Monocarp and Polycarp are learning new programming techniques. Now they decided to try pair programming.

It's known that they have worked together on the same file for n + m minutes. Every minute exactly one of them made one change to the file. Before they started, there were already k lines written in the file.

Every minute exactly one of them does one of two actions: adds a new line to the end of the file or changes one of its lines.

Monocarp worked in total for n minutes and performed the sequence of actions [a_1, a_2, ..., a_n]. If a_i = 0, then he adds a new line to the end of the file. If a_i > 0, then he changes the line with the number a_i. Monocarp performed actions strictly in this order: a_1, then a_2, ..., a_n.

Polycarp worked in total for m minutes and performed the sequence of actions [b_1, b_2, ..., b_m]. If b_j = 0, then he adds a new line to the end of the file. If b_j > 0, then he changes the line with the number b_j. Polycarp performed actions strictly in this order: b_1, then b_2, ..., b_m.

Restore their common sequence of actions of length n + m such that all actions would be correct — there should be no changes to lines that do not yet exist. Keep in mind that in the common sequence Monocarp's actions should form the subsequence [a_1, a_2, ..., a_n] and Polycarp's — subsequence [b_1, b_2, ..., b_m]. They can replace each other at the computer any number of times.

Let's look at an example. Suppose k = 3. Monocarp first changed the line with the number 2 and then added a new line (thus, n = 2, \: a = [2, 0]). Polycarp first added a new line and then changed the line with the number 5 (thus, m = 2, \: b = [0, 5]).

Since the initial length of the file was 3, in order for Polycarp to change line number 5 two new lines must be added beforehand. Examples of correct sequences of changes, in this case, would be [0, 2, 0, 5] and [2, 0, 0, 5]. Changes [0, 0, 5, 2] (wrong order of actions) and [0, 5, 2, 0] (line 5 cannot be edited yet) are not correct.

Input

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Then t test cases follow. Before each test case, there is an empty line.

Each test case contains three lines. The first line contains three integers k, n, m (0 ≤ k ≤ 100, 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100) — the initial number of lines in file and lengths of Monocarp's and Polycarp's sequences of changes respectively.

The second line contains n integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n (0 ≤ a_i ≤ 300).

The third line contains m integers b_1, b_2, ..., b_m (0 ≤ b_j ≤ 300).

6 0 8 0
0 7 0 9

5 4 1

0

0 2 0 6 5

original_problem_description:
Valeric and Valerko missed the last Euro football game, so they decided to watch the game's key moments on the Net. They want to start watching as soon as possible but the connection speed is too low. If they turn on the video right now, it will "hang up" as the size of data to watch per second will be more than the size of downloaded data per second.

The guys want to watch the whole video without any pauses, so they have to wait some integer number of seconds for a part of the video to download. After this number of seconds passes, they can start watching. Waiting for the whole video to download isn't necessary as the video can download after the guys started to watch.

Let's suppose that video's length is c seconds and Valeric and Valerko wait t seconds before the watching. Then for any moment of time t0, t ≤ t0 ≤ c + t, the following condition must fulfill: the size of data received in t0 seconds is not less than the size of data needed to watch t0 - t seconds of the video.

Of course, the guys want to wait as little as possible, so your task is to find the minimum integer number of seconds to wait before turning the video on. The guys must watch the video without pauses.

Input

The first line contains three space-separated integers a, b and c (1 ≤ a, b, c ≤ 1000, a > b). The first number (a) denotes the size of data needed to watch one second of the video. The second number (b) denotes the size of data Valeric and Valerko can download from the Net per second. The third number (c) denotes the video's length in seconds.

Output

Print a single number — the minimum integer number of seconds that Valeric and Valerko must wait to watch football without pauses.

Examples

Input

4 1 1


Output

3


Input

10 3 2


Output

5


Input

13 12 1


Output

1

Note

In the first sample video's length is 1 second and it is necessary 4 units of data for watching 1 second of video, so guys should download 4 · 1 = 4 units of data to watch the whole video. The most optimal way is to wait 3 seconds till 3 units of data will be downloaded and then start watching. While guys will be watching video 1 second, one unit of data will be downloaded and Valerik and Valerko will have 4 units of data by the end of watching. Also every moment till the end of video guys will have more data then necessary for watching.

In the second sample guys need 2 · 10 = 20 units of data, so they have to wait 5 seconds and after that they will have 20 units before the second second ends. However, if guys wait 4 seconds, they will be able to watch first second of video without pauses, but they will download 18 units of data by the end of second second and it is less then necessary.

```python
import sys
from collections import Counter

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if len(data) < 2:

    k = int(data[0])
    s = data[1]
    freq = Counter(s)
    # تحقق من قابلية القسمة
    for cnt in freq.values():

            sys.stdout.write('-1')
            return
    # بناء النمط الأساسي بترتيب أبجدي

    for ch in sorted(freq.keys()):

    sys.stdout.write(result)
```


original_problem_description:
A string is called a k-string if it can be represented as k concatenated copies of some string. For example, the string "aabaabaabaab" is at the same time a 1-string, a 2-string and a 4-string, but it is not a 3-string, a 5-string, or a 6-string and so on. Obviously any string is a 1-string.

You are given a string s, consisting of lowercase English letters and a positive integer k. Your task is to reorder the letters in the string s in such a way that the resulting string is a k-string.

Input

The first input line contains integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 1000). The second line contains s, all characters in s are lowercase English letters. The string length s satisfies the inequality 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 1000, where |s| is the length of string s.

Output

Rearrange the letters in string s in such a way that the result is a k-string. Print the result on a single output line. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

If the solution doesn't exist, print "-1" (without quotes).

Examples

Input

2
aazz


Output

azaz


Input

3
abcabcabz


Output

-1

```java
        FastScanner fs = new FastScanner(System.in);
        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(new BufferedWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(System.out)));
        int t = fs.nextInt();
        while (t-- > 0) {
            int k = fs.nextInt();
            int n = fs.nextInt();
            int m = fs.nextInt();
            int[] a = new int[n];
            int[] b = new int[m];
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) a[i] = fs.nextInt();
            for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) b[i] = fs.nextInt();

            List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<>();
            int i = 0, j = 0;
            boolean possible = true;
            while (i < n || j < m) {
                boolean took = false;
                // أولوية إضافة سطر جديد إذا كان متاحاً
                if (i < n && a[i] == 0) {
                    result.add(0);
                    k++;
                    i++;
                    took = true;
                } else if (j < m && b[j] == 0) {
                    result.add(0);
                    k++;
                    j++;
                    took = true;
                } else {
                    // لا يوجد صفر، نبحث عن أصغر قيمة قابلة للتنفيذ
                    int valA = (i < n) ? a[i] : Integer.MAX_VALUE;
                    int valB = (j < m) ? b[j] : Integer.MAX_VALUE;
                    if (valA <= k && valA <= valB) {
                        result.add(valA);
                        i++;
                        took = true;
                    } else if (valB <= k) {
                        result.add(valB);
                        j++;
                        took = true;
                    }
                }
                if (!took) { // لا يمكن اتخاذ أي خطوة
                    possible = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!possible) {
                out.println(-1);
            } else {
                for (int idx = 0; idx < result.size(); idx++) {
                    out.print(result.get(idx));
                    if (idx + 1 < result.size()) out.print(' ');
                }
                out.println();
            }
        }
        out.flush();
    }

    // قارئ سريع للمدخلات
    static class FastScanner {
        private final BufferedReader br;
        private StringTokenizer st;
        FastScanner(InputStream is) {
            br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(is));
        }
        String next() throws IOException {
            while (st == null || !st.hasMoreElements()) {
                String line = br.readLine();
                if (line == null) return null;
                st = new StringTokenizer(line);
            }
            return st.nextToken();
        }
        int nextInt() throws IOException { return Integer.parseInt(next()); }
    }
}
```

original_problem_description:
Monocarp and Polycarp are learning new programming techniques. Now they decided to try pair programming.

It's known that they have worked together on the same file for n + m minutes. Every minute exactly one of them made one change to the file. Before they started, there were already k lines written in the file.

Every minute exactly one of them does one of two actions: adds a new line to the end of the file or changes one of its lines.

Monocarp worked in total for n minutes and performed the sequence of actions [a_1, a_2, ..., a_n]. If a_i = 0, then he adds a new line to the end of the file. If a_i > 0, then he changes the line with the number a_i. Monocarp performed actions strictly in this order: a_1, then a_2, ..., a_n.

Polycarp worked in total for m minutes and performed the sequence of actions [b_1, b_2, ..., b_m]. If b_j = 0, then he adds a new line to the end of the file. If b_j > 0, then he changes the line with the number b_j. Polycarp performed actions strictly in this order: b_1, then b_2, ..., b_m.

Restore their common sequence of actions of length n + m such that all actions would be correct — there should be no changes to lines that do not yet exist. Keep in mind that in the common sequence Monocarp's actions should form the subsequence [a_1, a_2, ..., a_n] and Polycarp's — subsequence [b_1, b_2, ..., b_m]. They can replace each other at the computer any number of times.

Let's look at an example. Suppose k = 3. Monocarp first changed the line with the number 2 and then added a new line (thus, n = 2, \: a = [2, 0]). Polycarp first added a new line and then changed the line with the number 5 (thus, m = 2, \: b = [0, 5]).

Since the initial length of the file was 3, in order for Polycarp to change line number 5 two new lines must be added beforehand. Examples of correct sequences of changes, in this case, would be [0, 2, 0, 5] and [2, 0, 0, 5]. Changes [0, 0, 5, 2] (wrong order of actions) and [0, 5, 2, 0] (line 5 cannot be edited yet) are not correct.

Input

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Then t test cases follow. Before each test case, there is an empty line.

Each test case contains three lines. The first line contains three integers k, n, m (0 ≤ k ≤ 100, 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 100) — the initial number of lines in file and lengths of Monocarp's and Polycarp's sequences of changes respectively.

The second line contains n integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n (0 ≤ a_i ≤ 300).

The third line contains m integers b_1, b_2, ..., b_m (0 ≤ b_j ≤ 300).

Output

For each test case print any correct common sequence of Monocarp's and Polycarp's actions of length n + m or -1 if such sequence doesn't exist.

0 5

4 3 2
2 0 5
0 6

1 0
2 3

5 4 4
6 0 8 0
0 7 0 9

5 4 1

0

-1

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int la, lb;
    if (!(cin >> la >> lb)) return 0;
    vector<int> A(la);
    for (int &x : A) cin >> x;
    vector<int> B(lb);
    // خريطة من العنصر إلى موقعه في الدائرة b
    const int MAXV = 1000000 + 5;
    vector<int> posInB(MAXV, -1);
    for (int i = 0; i < lb; ++i) {
        cin >> B[i];
        posInB[B[i]] = i; // لا توجد تكرارات داخل b
    }

    // نضاعف a للتعامل مع اللفّ
    vector<int> A2(2 * la);
    for (int i = 0; i < 2 * la; ++i) A2[i] = A[i % la];

    long long best = 0;               // النتيجة
    deque<long long> window;          // المواقع (معدلة بإضافة دورات من b)
    long long firstPos = -1;          // أول موقع في النافذة بعد تعديل

    for (int i = 0; i < 2 * la; ++i) {
        int val = A2[i];
        int p = (val < (int)posInB.size()) ? posInB[val] : -1;
        if (p == -1) {                 // العنصر غير موجود في b → نعيد ضبط النافذة
            window.clear();
            firstPos = -1;
            continue;
        }
        long long cur = p;
        // إذا كان هناك عنصر سابق في النافذة، نضمن أن يكون cur أكبر منه
        if (!window.empty()) {
            long long last = window.back();
            // نضيف دورات من b حتى يصبح cur أكبر من last
            if (cur <= last) {
                long long add = ((last - cur) / lb + 1) * (long long)lb;
                cur += add;
            }
        }
        window.push_back(cur);
        if (firstPos == -1) firstPos = cur; // أول موقع في النافذة
        // نحافظ على شرط الفرق < lb
        while (!window.empty() && cur - firstPos >= lb) {
            window.pop_front();
            if (!window.empty()) firstPos = window.front();
            else firstPos = -1;
        }
        // لا يجوز أن يتجاوز طول النافذة la (لأن a لا يمكن أن تستخدم أكثر من la عنصرًا)
        while ((int)window.size() > la) {
            window.pop_front();
            if (!window.empty()) firstPos = window.front();
            else firstPos = -1;
        }
        best = max(best, (long long)window.size());
    }

    cout << best << '\n';
    return 0;
}
```
هذا البرنامج يقرأ المدخلات، يبني خريطة المواقع في b، يضاعف a للتعامل مع اللفّ، ثم يستخدم نافذة متزايدة مع تعديل المواقع لضمان الترتيب الدائري. كل عملية داخل الحلقة هي O(1)، لذا يصبح التعقّب الكلي O(la + lb) مع استهلاك ذاكرة O(la + lb + قيمة الحد الأقصى للرموز).

original_problem_description:
Polycarpus enjoys studying Berland hieroglyphs. Once Polycarp got hold of two ancient Berland pictures, on each of which was drawn a circle of hieroglyphs. We know that no hieroglyph occurs twice in either the first or the second circle (but in can occur once in each of them).

Polycarpus wants to save these pictures on his laptop, but the problem is, laptops do not allow to write hieroglyphs circles. So Polycarp had to break each circle and write down all of its hieroglyphs in a clockwise order in one line. A line obtained from the first circle will be called a, and the line obtained from the second one will be called b.

There are quite many ways to break hieroglyphic circles, so Polycarpus chooses the method, that makes the length of the largest substring of string a, which occurs as a subsequence in string b, maximum.

Help Polycarpus — find the maximum possible length of the desired substring (subsequence) if the first and the second circles are broken optimally.

The length of string s is the number of characters in it. If we denote the length of string s as |s|, we can write the string as s = s1s2... s|s|.

A substring of s is a non-empty string x = s[a... b] = sasa + 1... sb (1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ |s|). For example, "code" and "force" are substrings of "codeforces", while "coders" is not. 

A subsequence of s is a non-empty string y = s[p1p2... p|y|] = sp1sp2... sp|y| (1 ≤ p1 < p2 < ... < p|y| ≤ |s|). For example, "coders" is a subsequence of "codeforces".

Input

The first line contains two integers la and lb (1 ≤ la, lb ≤ 1000000) — the number of hieroglyphs in the first and second circles, respectively.

Below, due to difficulties with encoding of Berland hieroglyphs, they are given as integers from 1 to 106.

The second line contains la integers — the hieroglyphs in the first picture, in the clockwise order, starting with one of them.

The third line contains lb integers — the hieroglyphs in the second picture, in the clockwise order, starting with one of them.

It is guaranteed that the first circle doesn't contain a hieroglyph, which occurs twice. The second circle also has this property.

Output

Print a single number — the maximum length of the common substring and subsequence. If at any way of breaking the circles it does not exist, print 0.

Examples

Input

5 4
1 2 3 4 5
1 3 5 6


Output

2


Input

4 6
1 3 5 2
1 2 3 4 5 6


Output

3


Input

3 3
1 2 3
3 2 1


Output

2

Note

In the first test Polycarpus picks a string that consists of hieroglyphs 5 and 1, and in the second sample — from hieroglyphs 1, 3 and 5.

original_problem_description:
Valeric and Valerko missed the last Euro football game, so they decided to watch the game's key moments on the Net. They want to start watching as soon as possible but the connection speed is too low. If they turn on the video right now, it will "hang up" as the size of data to watch per second will be more than the size of downloaded data per second.

The guys want to watch the whole video without any pauses, so they have to wait some integer number of seconds for a part of the video to download. After this number of seconds passes, they can start watching. Waiting for the whole video to download isn't necessary as the video can download after the guys started to watch.

Let's suppose that video's length is c seconds and Valeric and Valerko wait t seconds before the watching. Then for any moment of time t0, t ≤ t0 ≤ c + t, the following condition must fulfill: the size of data received in t0 seconds is not less than the size of data needed to watch t0 - t seconds of the video.

Of course, the guys want to wait as little as possible, so your task is to find the minimum integer number of seconds to wait before turning the video on. The guys must watch the video without pauses.

Input

The first line contains three space-separated integers a, b and c (1 ≤ a, b, c ≤ 1000, a > b). The first number (a) denotes the size of data needed to watch one second of the video. The second number (b) denotes the size of data Valeric and Valerko can download from the Net per second. The third number (c) denotes the video's length in seconds.

Output

Print a single number — the minimum integer number of seconds that Valeric and Valerko must wait to watch football without pauses.

Examples

Input

4 1 1


Output

3


Input

10 3 2


Output

5


Input

13 12 1


Output

1

Note

In the first sample video's length is 1 second and it is necessary 4 units of data for watching 1 second of video, so guys should download 4 · 1 = 4 units of data to watch the whole video. The most optimal way is to wait 3 seconds till 3 units of data will be downloaded and then start watching. While guys will be watching video 1 second, one unit of data will be downloaded and Valerik and Valerko will have 4 units of data by the end of watching. Also every moment till the end of video guys will have more data then necessary for watching.

In the second sample guys need 2 · 10 = 20 units of data, so they have to wait 5 seconds and after that they will have 20 units before the second second ends. However, if guys wait 4 seconds, they will be able to watch first second of video without pauses, but they will download 18 units of data by the end of second second and it is less then necessary.

A string is called a k-string if it can be represented as k concatenated copies of some string. For example, the string "aabaabaabaab" is at the same time a 1-string, a 2-string and a 4-string, but it is not a 3-string, a 5-string, or a 6-string and so on. Obviously any string is a 1-string.

Input

The first input line contains integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 1000). The second line contains s, all characters in s are lowercase English letters. The string length s satisfies the inequality 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 1000, where |s| is the length of string s.

Output

Rearrange the letters in string s in such a way that the result is a k-string. Print the result on a single output line. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.

If the solution doesn't exist, print "-1" (without quotes).

Examples

Input

2
aazz


Output

azaz


Input

abcabcabz
